closing_line: Evaluate with labeled tickets before enabling actions. Follow AI Daily Diff for verified builder updates.

items.headline: Evaluate a typed department answer before connecting your support application to actions.
items.what_changed: October 6 introduced the Decisions API beta with GPT-6 Luna.
items.why_it_matters: A routing label can feed application logic; classification itself is not new.

diff.minus: Existing structured-output workflows remain an option.
diff.plus: A dedicated endpoint offers fixed-choice answers.

items.watch_out: Handle refusals and review uncertain cases. We did not test this API live.

walkthrough.use_case: Proposed test: classify a fictional duplicate-charge ticket into payments, delivery, product support or other; no account action.
walkthrough.steps:
Use authorized API access; documented Python examples need SDK 3.26.0+.
Send model=gpt-6-luna, the ticket as input, and a named choice question to POST /v1/decisions.
Give each department a distinct value and description; include other for unmatched tickets.
Check answers for refusal before reading choice or confidence.
Compare with human labels and route ambiguous results to review. This evaluation was not executed.
walkthrough.availability: Public beta; gpt-6-luna only. API access and usage limits apply.
walkthrough.limitations: No live API test. Proposed evaluation does not establish accuracy, speed or production reliability.
walkthrough.evidence_label: Documentation reviewed; no live API test.

youtube_description:
OpenAI released the Decisions API beta on October 6. This builder briefing examines where a typed routing answer fits into a support application.

Our proposed evaluation uses fictional ticket messages and a human-labeled test set. Compare misroutes across categories, include ambiguous messages, and keep application actions disabled during evaluation. A valid category alone is not evidence of a correct business decision.

This is a documented walkthrough, not a live API test or a latency benchmark. Follow AI Daily Diff for verified technical changes and practical evaluation questions.
